propositions: Capability decisions for native_structured_output and prompt_cache_style are currently made via provider-name string matching (startswith checks), which fails for Bedrock-hosted Claude models whose capability flags diverge from the direct Anthropic API

Two code paths silently disable caching and structured output for Bedrock Claude: output_mode() checks _NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS frozenset and runner.py checks model string prefix, both missing the bedrock provider name

ModelProfile objects in pydantic-ai expose per-vendor capability records; replacing string matches with profile reads requires accepting both model objects (rebar-built providers) and lazy model strings (OpenAI, Google) to avoid breaking the S1 lazy-string contract and forcing optional SDKs to be importable

A rebar override table using profile predicates (not provider names) is load-bearing: anthropic_model_profile reports supports_json_schema_output=True for Claude on all hosts, but rebar's PromptedOutput path was deliberately chosen and must not be silently overridden

Bedrock capability detection must use field presence checks (bedrock_supports_prompt_caching, bedrock_thinking_variant) rather than isinstance(BedrockModelProfile) because BedrockModelProfile is in boto3-dependent pydantic_ai.models.bedrock and CI lacks the SDK, breaking the stdlib-only import contract

The groq provider is a disclosed behavior change: groq_model_profile reports supports_json_schema_output=False, contradicting today's _NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS inclusion, and will move from NativeOutput to PromptedOutput since the profile is the authoritative capability source
